claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by high-temperature consolidation can incorporate nanoscale Y2O3 particles into an RHEA matrix.
The intervention will produce a fine dispersion of nanoscale oxide particles within the RHEA matrix.
Dispersed oxide particles will pin grain boundaries in the RHEA.
Grain-boundary pinning by oxide particles will reduce grain growth at temperatures above 1000°C.
Dispersed oxide particles will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects in the RHEA.
The oxide-particle defect sinks will mitigate the accumulation of irradiation-induced dislocation loops.
The oxide-particle defect sinks will mitigate the accumulation of irradiation-induced voids.
The oxide-dispersed RHEA will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than an otherwise comparable RHEA without oxide dispersion.
The oxide-dispersed RHEA will have greater elevated-temperature creep resistance than the baseline RHEA.
The oxide-dispersed RHEA will exhibit less irradiation-induced swelling than the baseline RHEA.
The oxide-dispersed RHEA will exhibit less radiation-induced hardening than the baseline RHEA.
The oxide dispersion will maintain the RHEA's thermal stability under high-temperature exposure.
The oxide dispersion will maintain the RHEA's stability under neutron or ion irradiation.
Agglomeration of the oxide particles during processing would reduce their effectiveness for grain-boundary pinning and defect-sink behavior.
Particle size and spatial distribution must be optimized for effective grain-boundary pinning and defect-sink behavior.
